verdict.rationale: Running a Windows VM is a fair question for a desktop operating system, so the axis applies. However, the evidence pack never documents any virtualization capability on Ubuntu Desktop, such as a hypervisor, VM manager or guest OS support. The WSL items describe the reverse case, Ubuntu running inside Windows, and remote desktop sharing is a different feature, so neither counts toward this story.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run a full Windows environment in a virtual machine for apps not natively available
